knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A sealer reduces absorption and staining. It does not repair damage, fill cracks or hide defects.
Sealing over residue traps the contamination and can affect the finish and the cure.
Thin, even coats that follow the product data are the correct method. Thick coats trap solvent and can leave lines.
The client care note must give the written cure time, the approved cleaners and the re-seal interval.
The client should use only the cleaners listed in the product care guidance, because other cleaners can damage the finish.

practicalCriteria: Confirms the surface is clean, dry and tested before sealing
Applies thin, even coats that follow the product data
Records the product, batch and cure conditions
Gives the client a written care note at handover
passRule: Knowledge checks: 4 of 5 correct (80%). Practical sign-off is separate and is not granted by the knowledge check: an assessor must observe every critical practical criterion and record it.
evidenceRequired: Product and batch record with coat count and cure conditions
stopWorkCriteria: Surface not dry to the product requirement
Sealer not approved for the stone and finish
